lect: Shona (Zezuru-based verbal generalisations; harmony also reported in other dialects)
time_scope: modern descriptive data drawing on Fortune 1955
claim: Root-initial syllables permit the full vowel-height contrast, but non-initial non-low vowels are height-dependent: mid vowels /e, o/ occur non-initially only after a preceding mid vowel, while high vowels occur after high or low vowels but not after mid vowels.

source_forms.generalisation: leftmost mid vowel in a licit mid-vowel string must be root-initial

formal_environment: root-initial V1 ... noninitial Vn in verb roots/derived stems
normalized_environment: [high] contrast privileged root-initially; subsequent nonlow V harmonizes in height with harmonic licensor
scope: Shona verbs; Zezuru description used for examples
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Low /a/ is not governed by this simple alternation; the rounding-conditioned e...u exception is recorded separately.

time_scope: modern descriptive data drawing on Fortune 1955
claim: The height co-occurrence restrictions are maintained both inside polysyllabic verb roots and across root-suffix boundaries in derived stems; Beckman reports no polysyllabic verb roots that fail to exhibit the harmony generalisation.
normalized_environment: height harmony spans root-internal and derivational suffix domain
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Some listed extensions are synchronically unproductive; productivity status is lexical/morphological metadata, not evidence that the height pattern itself disappears in the cited forms.

time_scope: modern descriptive data drawing on Fortune 1955
claim: Low /a/ is opaque to height harmony: it remains low regardless of preceding height, blocks continuation of a mid-vowel harmony span, and is followed by high rather than mid vowels.

source_forms.distribution: after intervening a, further mid vowels do not occur; high vowels surface instead

normalized_environment: a blocks height spreading; post-a nonlow default is high
exceptions_or_counterexamples: This is specifically an opacity/blocking effect of low /a/, not transparency. Low vowels themselves are described as freely distributed in verbs.

time_scope: modern descriptive data drawing on Fortune 1955
claim: Height harmony is blocked when root-initial front mid /e/ is followed by a round vowel: disharmonic e...u is permitted where e...o would otherwise be expected, whereas round-initial /o/ requires following round non-low vowels to be mid.
formal_environment: root-initial e/o ... later round nonlow vowel
normalized_environment: height harmony conditioned by rounding agreement; e cannot license noninitial o across rounding mismatch
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Beckman calls #[CeCu] the sole exception to the simple local height-harmony generalisation summarized in (7); the effect is not a wholesale suspension of harmony after all mid vowels.
section: 3 Shona: data and generalisations; §5 rounding analysis
